21.0.0.en: After the death of Jehoshaphat and his burial in Jerusalem, his firstborn son Jehoram reigned, whom his father had prepared to reign after him, since he shared the rule with him for the last five years of Jehoshaphat's life. Jehoram had six brothers, for whom their father Jehoshaphat cared, so he gave them authority in the cities of Judah and also gave them gifts of gold, silver and precious things, that is, valuable gifts. This was so that no dispute over the kingdom would arise after his death, for it was an implicit declaration, in Jehoshaphat's lifetime, that Jehoram was the new king, or the crown prince. Sadly Jehoram was wicked, so he feared that his brothers would compete with him for the kingdom, or take it from him, especially since they were good and better than he (2 Chr 31:13), for the people might love them and submit to one of them, who would then compete with him for the kingdom; therefore he acted with violence and cruelty and killed all his brothers, and perhaps he devised a plot and dealt treacherously with them; indeed he also killed a number of the princes of his people, who may have been good men and lovers of his brothers.

21.0.1.en: And this heinous deed that Jehoram did was widespread among the pagan nations: whoever reigns kills his brothers, lest anyone compete with him for the kingdom, and perhaps Jehoram learned this thinking from his mother-in-law, the pagan Jezebel, or from his wife Athaliah, who was influenced by her pagan mother Jezebel.

21.0.2.en: And this shows the characteristics of Jehoram, that he was not good and a lover of the Lord and His commandments, otherwise he would not have killed his innocent brothers; indeed it also shows his being influenced by his wife and his mother-in-law in the worship of idols, which he cared for, as will appear in the following verses.

21.0.3.en: Do not yield to anxiety and fear so that you become troubled, and then think evil of others, or wrong them. Rely on God and ask for His help, and He will give you peace. Enjoy His fellowship in prayer and reading, and your relationship with others will improve and you will treat them kindly.

21.1.0.en: These verses are recorded and were explained in (2 Kgs 8:16-19), and in them we see the evils of King Jehoram, which were because of his marriage to Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab king of Israel. They were many evils, deserving that God should destroy him, but He was long-suffering with him for the sake of David his forefather, the righteous king.

21.2.s.en: (2) The revolt of Edom and Libnah against him

21.2.0.en: These verses are recorded and were explained in the Encyclopedia in (2 Kgs 8:20-22). And we see in them the Edomites' revolt against Jehoram by setting up a king over themselves, so he attacked them and triumphed over them at first, but they surrounded him, so he fled from them and the Edomites rebelled against him. Likewise the city of Libnah revolted, which lies in the kingdom of Judah and is inhabited by the priests, and God allowed this revolt because Jehoram had turned away from God and worshiped idols.

21.3.0.en: Asa, and then his son Jehoshaphat, took care of the worship of the Lord and the removal of the pagan forms of worship at the high places in the kingdom of Judah, but Jehoram did not walk in the way of his father Jehoshaphat and his forefather Asa; on the contrary, he made forms of worship for idols on the high places in the land of the kingdom of Judah. Only a group of wicked kings did this evil: Jeroboam king of Israel (1 Kgs 12:31) and Ahaz and Manasseh, kings of Judah (2 Chr 28:25, 2 Kgs 21:3). And by building these high places, Jehoram led the people of God away from His worship and cast them into the mazes of idolatry, because by this they became spiritual fornicators, by forsaking God and worshiping strange gods, and they might fall into bodily fornication to please these gods, because it was part of the rites of their worship. And in this evil in which Jehoram walked, his wife Athaliah played a great part, and also his mother-in-law Jezebel, because they were idol worshipers.

21.3.1.en: Know that every bad thought, or evil word you say, or any wicked deed, takes you away from God, so hasten to repent and do what pleases God, draw near to Him by prayer, reading the Holy Bible and every good work.

21.4.0.en: Elijah sent a letter to Jehoram king of Judah, in which he declared to him that the God of his father David was angry with him because he did not walk in the upright way in which his fathers Jehoshaphat and Asa had walked. Here he reminds him that the measure he should have set before him was his great forefather David, and then his forefather Asa and his father Jehoshaphat; he should have followed the example of their goodness, but sadly he walked in evil.

21.4.1.en: And it is important to know that Elijah went up to heaven during the life of Jehoshaphat, but in the spirit of prophecy he wrote this letter and charged his disciple Elisha the prophet to send it to Jehoram, perhaps that he would be affected by it and repent; and if he did not obey God, this letter would be a witness against him. But sadly Jehoram did not obey the word of God, so he became worse than Ahab his father-in-law, the most wicked of the kings of Israel, who did many evils, but when Elijah warned him he repented, so God postponed the punishment until after his death.

21.5.0.en: God specified to Jehoram his chief evils, which are:

21.5.1.en: 1- His evil conduct like the kings of Israel, that is, the worship of idols and all the sins connected with it, such as fornication.

21.5.2.en: 2- His causing his people to stumble, in turning them away from the worship of God and making them fall into the worship of idols.

21.5.3.en: 3- His killing his good brothers, who were better than he, in order to rule alone; because their presence shows his sins by comparison with them, and he would be exposed to being deposed by the people. By this he shed innocent blood.

21.6.0.en: God declared his punishment to him, that he might repent and God forgive him, or so that when the punishment happened he would not think it a coincidence, but know that it was the wrath of God; but sadly he did not respond to God's warnings. And this punishment is:

21.6.1.en: 1- God strikes Jehoram's wives and his sons and all that he has, and this happened at the hands of the Philistines, before Jehoram's eyes (v. 17); as he killed his brothers, God allowed his sons to be killed (ch. 22:1).

21.6.2.en: 2- God strikes the wives of the people of Judah, who followed the king in the worship of idols.

21.6.3.en: 3- God strikes Jehoram himself with a serious disease in his bowels, so that they come out of him while he is alive, and he dies.

21.6.4.en: And it seems that because of Jehoram's evils, which filled his heart, God allowed him to be struck in his bowels, so his bowels came out of him gradually for two years until he died (vv. 18, 19); all this is long-suffering from God, to give him an opportunity to repent.

21.6.5.en: God is wonderful in His long-suffering, for He gives us opportunity after opportunity to repent. May we seize these opportunities and return to Him, and so escape destruction.

21.7.s.en: (4) The attack of the Philistines and the Arabs, then the death of Jehoram

21.7.0.en: The Arabs that are near the Ethiopians (Cushites): the Cushites lived in the land of Abyssinia and some of them migrated to the south of the Arabian Peninsula, that is, present-day Yemen; so the Arabs living near them are those who lived in the south of the Arabian Peninsula, that is, present-day Saudi Arabia.

21.7.1.en: Because of Jehoram's persistence in his evils, God abandoned him and allowed the Philistines and the Arabs to rise against him and attack him. How hard it is for God to be angry with a person and stir up others against him. The Philistines and the Arabs were violent, so their attack was severe.

21.7.2.en: Do not persist in your sins and so defy God, and then He abandons you, and you become an easy prey for demons and the wicked, who torment you. Hasten to repentance, for it is your only way to escape.

21.8.0.en: The Philistines and the Arabs attacked the kingdom of Judah and concentrated on the capital of the kingdom, so they attacked the king, and perhaps they could not kill him because of the guards who guarded him, but they entered his palaces and took his wives and sons captive, and plundered his wealth also.

21.8.1.en: And this is the natural end of the wicked, to lose everything: as he stole the share of his brothers and killed them, the wicked attacked him and plundered all his wealth, and even humbled him by taking his wives and sons.

21.9.0.en: After Jehoram became poor, humbled and alone, God also struck him with a serious disease, without healing, in his bowels, which began to come out of him gradually outside his body. And he was afflicted with many diseases, which continued for two years. And the diseases in the end led him to death. Thus Elijah's prophecy was fulfilled in him (v. 15). And we see the hardness of the wicked Jehoram's heart in the following:

21.9.1.en: 1- Refusing to learn from the prayers of his father Jehoshaphat and his fear of God.

21.9.2.en: 2- Refusing to submit to the Law of God, which his father Jehoshaphat took care to teach to all his people.

21.9.3.en: 3- Refusing to submit to Elijah's letter and warnings, and perhaps Athaliah his wife encouraged him in this, and she may have burned this letter with contempt and scorn, and kept him away from the Law of God and from praying to Him.

21.9.4.en: 4- After Elijah's prophecy was fulfilled in him, and it was in stages, his heart was not affected and he did not return to God, for his wealth was plundered and his wives and sons were taken captive, then the disease struck him and continued for two years, and in all this he refused to repent, so he died and went to destruction.

21.9.5.en: Because of Jehoram's evils his people did not love him, because whoever kills his brothers is of course a person of utmost selfishness and cruelty, and consequently is cruel and unjust to his people. And the people, especially the good among them, would have preferred that one of Jehoram's good brothers reign over them, who were influenced by the goodness of Jehoshaphat and his prayer and teachings, and were troubled by Jehoram's spreading of the worship of idols. All this made them feel distress at Jehoram, so when he died they did not make an honor for him like the rest of the kings; they did not make for him the great burning, in which they used to put spices, which gave a pleasant sight and fragrance, because Jehoram's life was evil and foul and had nothing good in it, so they did not mourn his death.

21.10.0.en: Jehoram reigned alone on the throne when he was thirty-two years old and reigned for eight years, but he had also reigned five years before that with his father Jehoshaphat, so the total of his reign was thirteen years (2 Kgs 8:16). And he died at about forty years old. And because of the people's distress at him, they buried him in the city of David, but did not bury him in the tombs of the kings his fathers, although there were wicked kings before him, such as Rehoboam and Abijah, but Jehoram's evils were greater than theirs, so they did not bury him with them. And this signifies the separation of the wicked from the righteous at the end of the days, that is, the wicked will be separated and cast into eternal torment.

21.10.1.en: Ahaziah, and then Athaliah, reign over Judah

24.0.s.en: (3) The death of Jehoiada and Joash's apostasy from the Lord

24.0.0.en: God prolonged the life of Jehoiada, so he lived longer than was usual in his days, for he lived 130 years, and so he was born in the days of King Solomon and lived in the time of nine kings, the first of whom was Solomon and the last Joash, and he enjoyed the goodness that prevailed in the days of Asa and Jehoshaphat. All this was a preparation by God for him, to play a great role, which was the care of the child king Joash, whom he raised when he was one year old, then crowned and anointed king when he was seven years old, and continued to care for him and guide him, so he worshiped the Lord and carried out the restoration of the temple, so that he even reproached Jehoiada himself for his lack of zeal in collecting silver for the restoration of the temple. Although Jehoiada had some excuse, because his age at that time was nearly 130 years. Thus the importance of the priestly role in the Book of Chronicles appears, because the goodness in the first part of the life of King Joash is owed to Jehoiada

24.1.0.en: In honor of the great Jehoiada, to whom is owed the goodness of the kingdom in the days of Joash, and perhaps his goodness preserved the temple even in the days of the wicked kings; therefore they buried him with honor in the city of David beside the kings, and perhaps they wrote on his tomb that he "did good with God and His house," so they distinguished him by burying him with the kings.

24.2.0.en: After the death of Jehoiada a group of the princes of Judah came to King Joash, whose minds were corrupted and who loved the worship of idols, and they are those who lived in the days of Jehoram, Ahaziah and Athaliah, the wicked kings. And they showed their submission to the king by bowing down to him, and perhaps they flattered him; indeed they showed him that he had been rid of the high priest, who had controlled him, and that he was free now to do what he saw fit and to seek help from the other gods and benefit from them, as all the nations around him worship them. And they continued in their talk until they convinced him, so he agreed to establish the worship of idols, by offering worship at the groves and the images of idols, and they neglected the worship of the Lord, so the Lord was angry with them.

24.3.0.en: God was long-suffering with His people in the kingdom of Judah and sent them prophets to guide them and bring them back to God, but sadly they rejected the word of God and continued in their evil and their worship of idols. This shows that God does not leave Himself without a witness, and also shows the people's persistence and insistence on evil.

24.4.0.en: God also warned His people through Zechariah the priest the son of Jehoiada, for the Spirit of God came upon him, and he stood on a high platform, so he was higher than all the people, and called to all who were gathered that they should turn from the worship of idols and worship God, and he showed the extent of their evil and their betrayal of God, and warned them that their forsaking God would expose them to God's abandoning them and consequently failure in all their life. And this warning of his is from the Law of God (Deut 29:25, 31:16, 17), that is, he conveyed the word of God to them so that they might repent.

24.4.1.en: And perhaps this Zechariah is the one mentioned in the New Testament, of whom Christ said that he was Zechariah the son of Barachias (Mt 23:35), because Jehoiada is also called Barachias.

24.5.0.en: When the wicked princes and the people, who clung to the worship of idols, heard the words of Zechariah, they reported him to King Joash, since he had transgressed his commands and was teaching the people against the king's words, so Joash commanded that Zechariah be killed, and they stoned him while he was teaching in the court of the house of the Lord. And this shows the extent of the evil to which Joash descended, so that he became a resister of the word of God and was led to the worship of idols.

24.6.0.en: Joash's killing of Zechariah shows his betrayal of God and his lack of appreciation for the kindness of Jehoiada, who raised him and preserved him, instead of his dying at the hand of Athaliah, and indeed crowned him king and guided him in the administration of the kingdom, so he succeeded and worshiped the Lord.

24.6.1.en: And at the death of Zechariah he said in the spirit of prophecy, "The LORD look upon it, and require it." He does not want God's vengeance on them, but rebukes them in the last moments of his life, perhaps they would repent, but sadly they refused to hear the word of God, so only a year passed and the Arameans attacked and triumphed over them, and the Lord struck Joash with disease. And what confirms that Zechariah's words are a prophecy that was fulfilled more than once is that Christ Himself referred to Zechariah and God's requiring his blood when He said, "All the righteous blood shed upon the earth shall come upon this generation, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar" (Mt 23:35).

24.6.2.en: God moved Zechariah to alert the people to the words of the Law so that they would repent. And God alerts you in many ways so that you return to Him, so do not persist in your sins and reject the word of God, because He loves you and seeks your salvation.

24.7.s.en: (4) The attack of the Arameans and the death of Joash

24.7.0.en: At the end of the year: after about a year.

24.7.1.en: After the prophecy of Zechariah the son of Jehoiada, at his death, only a year passed and the armies of the Arameans attacked the kingdom of Judah and killed the princes of the people, who had turned King Joash toward the worship of idols, and then plundered everything precious in Judah and Jerusalem and sent it to the capital of their king, Damascus.

24.7.2.en: And so we see God's abandoning His rebellious people, so He allows the killing of the wicked princes of the people and the plundering of the spoil of the kingdom, that His people may become poor, perhaps by this they would repent and return to God.

24.8.0.en: A small company: a small group.

24.8.1.en: They executed judgment: they ruled and humbled and punished.

24.8.2.en: To declare His severe abandoning of His people, God allowed a small number of Arameans to attack, and a great army from the kingdom of Judah confronted them but was defeated before them, because God wanted to punish the kingdom of Judah by the hand of their enemies the Arameans, and to humble His people He made them be defeated before a small group. And this is the opposite of God's work with His people when they hold fast to Him, as He was with them in the days of Jehoshaphat, when they triumphed over a huge army of the alliance of the Moabites, the Ammonites and the Edomites, without fighting them (ch. 20:20-25).

24.8.3.en: The power of God is available to you, if you believe in it and hold fast to God's commandments, but if you rebel against God and neglect His commandments, He abandons you, and the wicked despise you and humble you. Why do you give up your standing as the king's son? Rise quickly and return to God, to regain your sonship.

24.9.0.en: After the Arameans plundered Jerusalem and the king's palace, they found Joash sick with severe diseases, so they left him.

24.9.1.en: And as a punishment from God, two of Joash's servants rose against him and killed him while he was asleep on his bed. And this punishment was because of his killing innocent souls, the sons of Jehoiada: Zechariah the priest and his brothers. And this shows the extent of Joash's cruelty and his plunging into the worship of idols, and consequently his deserving the severe punishment that came upon him and his kingdom and his wicked princes. And God punished the whole kingdom, because they strayed from God and worshiped idols. And when the people felt the evil that had come upon them because of Joash, they did not bury him, when he died, in the tombs of the kings, but buried him with the common people, in the city of David.

24.9.2.en: It is noticed that the two killers of the king were of Gentile origin, that is, of the offspring of Moab and the children of Ammon, and this shows the extent of the spread of marriages contrary to the Law, that is, marrying Gentile women, so the king deserved this punishment.

24.10.0.en: The burdens laid upon him: what God punished him with, or the punishment that came upon him.

24.10.1.en: Midrash: a book of interpretation containing sermons.

24.10.2.en: The rest of the acts of King Joash and of his sons, and the divine punishments that came upon him, and all the accounts of his restoration of the house of the Lord, were written in the book of the Book of Kings, which is a historical book different from the Book of Kings that is in the Holy Bible; then his son Amaziah reigned on the throne of Judah after the death of his father Joash. Amaziah king of Judah
